examples.label: Fingerprint Drupal in the page source
Read CHANGELOG.txt for the exact version

notes: CHANGELOG.txt is the quickest exact-version tell but is often removed on hardened installs; fall back to /node/1 rendering and droopescan fingerprints. Version dictates which Drupalgeddon works.

recommended.note: Older Drupal: enable the PHP filter and drop a webshell.

name: Drupal - Detect and Version Enumeration
description: Confirms Drupal (page source, /node/1) and reads the version from CHANGELOG.txt; droopescan automates deeper module enumeration.

defense.why_it_works: Drupal exposes its identity through /CHANGELOG.txt (exact version), the generator meta tag, /node/ enumeration, /robots.txt for admin paths. All are unauthenticated.
defense.prerequisites: HTTP access to the site. No credentials required.
defense.impact: Version confirmation enables precise CVE targeting: Drupalgeddon (SA-CORE-2014-005), Drupalgeddon2 (CVE-2018-7600), Drupalgeddon3 (CVE-2018-7602).
defense.detection: Sequential GET requests to /CHANGELOG.txt, /node/1, /robots.txt. droopescan User-Agent in access logs.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (enumeration GETs to CHANGELOG.txt) | WAF alerts for CMS scanner patterns
defense.prevention: Remove CHANGELOG.txt, README.txt, INSTALL.txt from production. Restrict /admin to known IPs. Keep Drupal and modules updated.
defense.misconfiguration: Drupal deployed with default CHANGELOG.txt in web root, revealing exact version to unauthenticated users.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Default Drupal webroot includes:
# CHANGELOG.txt, README.txt, INSTALL.txt
# /node/1 accessible without auth
defense.evasion: Rename/obfuscate the uploaded webshell and delete it after use; prefer the app's built-in functionality (PHP filter / module) over dropping files; pace requests to blend with normal traffic.
